title: Hiking route card: photo with scrim, one action, unit-bearing stats and a route thumbnail
contains_third_party_content: Mountain photograph (origin unknown); place names appear fictional.

observed.layout: A white outer card holds an inner photo card of a golden-hour mountain. Bottom-left on the photo: 'Embercrest Ridge' (white, semibold) and 'Silverpine Mountains' (lighter). Bottom-right: a wide frosted dark pill 'Directions'. Under the photo: 'Hard', the line '1886 by Helen Rowe & Elias Mendez', a hairline, then three stats with units inside the values (12.4km, 870m, 4h 45m) and small grey labels (Distance, Elevation, Duration). Right: a light rounded tile with a looped route line and a dot.
observed.hierarchy: Photo, then title, then the 'Directions' action, then the stats.
observed.typography: Neutral grotesque; semibold title, light-grey labels. Typeface unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Photo with a dark gradient scrim at its base; frosted translucent button; concentric radii.

interpretation.aesthetic: Calm, premium outdoor; nested concentric radii (outer card, photo card, button, tile).
implementation_notes: Linear-gradient scrim over the photo base.
Frosted button via backdrop-filter and a low-alpha fill.
Stat row as a three-column grid.

concept_work.essence: The photo carries the emotion; units inside the values make the facts unambiguous.
what_makes_it_work: A scrim keeps overlaid text readable.
The route thumbnail answers 'what shape is this hike'.
gaps_to_make_it_work: '1886 by ...' is ambiguous (first ascent? first mapped?).
Stat labels measure about 2.06-2.41:1 (small light grey on white).

shared_tokens: three-up stat row with units in values
links: The route tile and the stat row describe the same route.
The Directions button leads from the card to navigation.

risks: Legibility of the frosted button over varied photos

pattern.name: Place card with stat strip
use_when: Trails, venues and listings with a few hard facts
adaptation_examples: Cycling route card: distance, climb, time, with a map tile.
Restaurant card: price band, wait, rating.

related.relation: header photo with a stat trio

lessons: Put units inside stat values and give every rating a scale.
Pair overlaid text with a scrim.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Warm photo against a cold-white UI; the only UI colors are white, black and grey.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: A place card whose job and action are obvious.
The photo and clean white UI are well balanced.
Units are inside values, but 'Hard' has no scale and the attribution line is ambiguous.
One clear action; no active, loading or error states shown.
Concentric radii and spacing are consistent.
A well-made but familiar card pattern.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 6.94:1; secondary text min 1.98:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
